chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdillah ibn Miskan, from Yahya al-Halbi, from Abd al-Hamid al-Ta'i, from Zurara ibn A'yan, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Can I marry a Murji'ah or a Haruriyyah?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Yes, marry the simple-minded one from the women.'
Zurara said, 'I said, 'By Allah, she is nothing but a believer or an infidel.'
So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'And where are the people of Thana' Allah (the dualists) Mighty and Majestic?'
The Words of Allah Mighty and Majestic: 'Except the weak from among the men and the women and the children who cannot devise a means nor are they guided a way.'
'[They are] more truthful than your words.'

key_terms.أَهْلُ ثَنْوَى: The people of Thana' (dualism/separation), referring to those who distinguish between belief and disbelief in a way that excludes certain groups.
key_terms.حَرُورِيَّةٍ: A member of the Haruriyyah (Khawarij) sect, known for excommunicating sinners.
key_terms.مُرْجِئَةٍ: A member of the Murji'ah sect, known for postponing judgment on sins.

ai.seo_question: Can I marry a woman from a different Islamic sect like the Murji'ah or Haruriyyah?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) permits marrying women from the Murji'ah and Haruriyyah sects, clarifying that their theological deviations do not constitute absolute disbelief (kufr dhihi) but rather a state of doubt or error. He cites the Quranic exception for the 'weak' (al-mustad'afin) who are unable to emigrate or find a way out, applying this principle to those whose faith is mixed with error but not entirely lost. This ruling highlights the Shia distinction between major theological sects and polytheists, emphasizing practical marital permissibility over strict doctrinal purity in this context.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muskan, from Yahya Al Halby, from Abdul Hameed Al Ta’aiy, from Zurara Bin Ayn who said,
‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Can I marry with a Murjiite or a Harouriyya (two sects)?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, but upon you is the simple one from the women’.
Zurara said, ‘I said, ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, what is she except for a Believing woman, or an Infidel’.
So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And where would be the dualist people about Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic?

The Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic are more truthful than your words, [4:98] Except the weak from among the men and the children who have not in their power the means nor can they find a way (to escape)’.
en.sarwar: 2. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muskan from Yahya al-Halabiy from ‘Abd al-Hamid al-Ta’iy from Zurarah ibn ‘A‘yan who has said the following:
“This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, if I can marry a Murji’ah or Harawriyah (two sects). He (the Imam) said, ‘No, but you must marry simple hearted woman.’
I then said, ‘By Allah, it is only a believer or unbeliever.’
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said, ‘What is the position of Thanawiy (a sect) people about Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious?
The words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, are truer than what you say “. . . except the weak ones of man, woman and children who cannot plan or find guidance to the right path. . . ’”
